newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - April 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - April 10.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on April 10:

WASHINGTON - The CIA revealed it had received numerous warnings starting in 1984 that chemical weapons were stored in a remote Iraqi ammunition depot that U.S. troops blew up shortly after the Persian Gulf War, but said it had failed to adequately alert the military to the danger.
ABIDJAN, Ivory Coast - Zairian rebels pushed into the country's second-largest city and President Mobutu Sese Seko turned to the military in an attempt to maintain his slipping hold on power.
WASHINGTON - A vast ocean once flowed beneath the icy surface of Jupiter's moon Europa and might still be flowing today as an incubator of extra-terrestrial life, scientists reported.

WASHINGTON - With a passionate vision of Washington as a "good city getting better", Mayor Marion Barry defended his administration's efforts to fix the broken gears of the government and boost the spirits of District residents.

WASHINGTON - The District government has budgeted nearly $7.3 million over the past three years for job-training programs, but not a single person has received training because city officials used the money to pay for salaries, benefits and outside contracts.

WASHINGTON - Hoping to jump-start the nation's effort to move large waves of welfare recipients into the work force, President Clinton will announce that the federal government will hire thousands of new employees off public assistance rolls.
